Plugins that change a callee-saved register

A plugin that returns with a callee-saved register changed breaks its host later and somewhere else. The host core now guards every plugin call, records the first change, and the qualification offers such a plugin isolated only.
Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, arm64) and an x86-64 desktop, October 2026; omx-clap-core 0.26.2.
What is done with such a plugin
What the guard does not show

What happens

Every calling convention gives a callee registers it must hand back as it found them:

  • aarch64: x19 to x28, d8 to d15, FPCR
  • x86-64: rbx, rbp, r12 to r15, MXCSR's control bits, the x87 control word

A caller may keep a value in one of them across the call. A plugin that returns with one changed replaces that value without anything crashing at the time. The damage shows later, somewhere else.

How it was found

Four limiter plugins of one LV2 collection, measured on a Raspberry Pi 5, returned from run() with d14 and d15 changed, from block 227 of the measurer's control sweep on, in 386 of its calls. The measurer kept its sample rate in d15. Its next instance was opened at 0 Hz, the plugin sized a buffer from that rate and wrote through a NULL pointer: each of the four was recorded as a crash (SIGSEGV).

Built at -O0, where the compiler keeps its locals in memory rather than in those registers, the measurer ran them to the end. At -O2 it crashed every time. That difference is the mark of a clobbered register.

The guard

The host core calls every plugin function through one guard, omx_abi_call6 (abi_guard.S):

  • it saves the callee-saved registers, calls, compares, and puts them back;
  • it records the first call that changed any: the registers, the plugin function and the run block.

Its cost is 14 to 15 ns per call on a Raspberry Pi 5 and 5.6 ns on an x86-64 desktop. For 24 plugins at 48 kHz in 256-frame blocks that is 0.36 µs of each 5,333 µs block.

The LV2 measurer makes every plugin call through the same guard, lilv_plugin_instantiate and lilv_instance_free included. Its record carries abi, for example:

{"clobbered":true,"registers":["d14","d15"],"call":"run","block":227,"calls":386}

A plugin that never clobbered reads {"clobbered":false}.

What is done with such a plugin

The verdict is hosting.stability.callee-saved-clobbered, rated conditional: the plugin is offered isolated only, in a worker of its own, never in-process in the console and never in a shared chain. The guard keeps the host's own frame whole; it does not protect the state of other plugins in the same process.

A worker reports abi_clobber <instance> <mask> <registers> <call> <block> on its feedback port, once per instance, and plugin-hostd then moves the instance, with its state, to a worker of its own.

Under the guard the four limiters measure to the end: no allocation in run(), and every rate sounds. Their figures from before the guard may have been corrupted and are not used.

What the guard does not show

A plugin that crashed without the guard and runs to the end with it, recording no clobber, is not proven clean: the guard changes the measurer's stack frame and may hide a memory fault. And a plugin that still crashes under the guard and at -O0 has its cause elsewhere.

How to see it again

The test fixture native/fixtures/lv2-gain.c of plugin-qualify, built with -DFIXTURE_ABI_BREAKER, returns from its third run() with x19 and d15 changed (rbx and r15 on x86-64), in assembly, after the C run() has returned. The test src/lv2-measure-native.test.ts measures it to the end and checks the record.
